documents.title: Seismicity of the 2015 Axial Seamount eruption recorded by the Regional Cabled Array
documents.abstract: We analyze the seismic swarm accompanying the April 2015 eruption of Axial Seamount using the OOI Regional Cabled Array. Thousands of volcanic earthquakes and inflation-deflation cycles are tracked in near real time, constraining magma migration beneath the caldera.

documents.title: Methane hydrate bubble plume dynamics at Southern Hydrate Ridge
documents.abstract: Continuous cabled observations resolve the temporal variability of methane bubble plumes emanating from Southern Hydrate Ridge. Plume flux correlates with bottom pressure and tidal forcing, informing models of gas hydrate dissociation on the Cascadia margin.

documents.title: Ambient noise cross-correlation and velocity monitoring offshore Cascadia
documents.abstract: We apply ambient noise interferometry to continuous records from the cabled array to retrieve empirical Green's functions between ocean-bottom stations. Seasonal velocity changes are monitored via coda-wave interferometry, demonstrating crustal monitoring capability in the offshore environment.

documents.title: Noise characterization of broadband ocean-bottom seismometers on a cabled network
documents.abstract: The noise floor of broadband OBS deployed on the Regional Cabled Array is characterized across the microseism band. Infragravity waves and current-induced tilt dominate long-period noise, with implications for ambient noise cross-correlation and event detection.

documents.title: The OOI Regional Cabled Array: infrastructure for real-time seafloor science
documents.abstract: An overview of the Ocean Observatories Initiative Regional Cabled Array, a fiber-optic observatory spanning the Juan de Fuca plate. We describe power and timing, instrument complement, and data delivery enabling multidisciplinary real-time seafloor observations.

documents.title: Tremor and low-frequency earthquakes on the Cascadia subduction megathrust
documents.abstract: Cabled and land seismic data are combined to locate tectonic tremor and low-frequency earthquakes downdip of the locked Cascadia megathrust. Offshore stations extend detection updip, improving constraints on slow-slip migration.

documents.title: Seafloor pressure records and tsunami detection on the cabled array
documents.abstract: High-sample-rate bottom pressure recorders on the Regional Cabled Array capture the seafloor deformation and tsunami waveforms of distant earthquakes. We assess real-time tsunami detection thresholds for offshore Cascadia.

documents.title: Machine learning detection of seismic events on the OOI cabled array
documents.abstract: A convolutional neural network is trained to detect and classify seismic events in continuous cabled-array data. The model improves catalog completeness for microearthquakes and volcanic signals relative to STA/LTA baselines.

documents.title: Water-column temperature and dissolved oxygen time series from cabled moorings
documents.abstract: Multi-year time series of temperature and dissolved oxygen from cabled moorings reveal hypoxic events on the Oregon shelf. Physical drivers including upwelling and internal tides are quantified.

documents.title: Fin whale vocalizations recorded on ocean-bottom seismometers
documents.abstract: Fin whale calls are detected on cabled ocean-bottom seismometers and used to study seasonal presence and call rates. Overlap of whale calls with the microseism band is discussed for seismic noise studies.
